title: Visit note

sentences.text: You came in for a follow-up visit for your long-term lower back pain.
You said your pain has been worse this past month.
You described your pain as a dull ache, about 4 out of 10 on most days.
The pain goes down your right leg, mostly after sitting for about an hour.
You had to leave work early two times this month.
You wake up 3 to 4 times a night because of pain, and you often feel tired.
You said a heating pad and stretching before bed help you sleep.
You have had no weakness, trouble walking, or bladder or bowel problems.
You go to physical therapy once a week and have gone for about 6 to 7 weeks. The core exercises help.
You do your home exercises 3 days a week.
When Dr. Lee raised your left leg, you felt pain down the back of the leg.
Your reflexes and strength were normal.
Your MRI from last year showed a bulging disc in your lower back.
These findings point to an irritated nerve in your lower back.
Gabapentin: increased to 600 mg three times a day.
Meloxicam 15 mg once a day with breakfast. No change.
Acetaminophen (Tylenol) as needed in the evening, about 2 to 3 times a week. No change.
Gabapentin makes you a little dizzy in the morning, and it goes away in about an hour.
Referral to Dr. Patel at the Spine Center for an evaluation. They may order an MRI.
Keep going to physical therapy once a week and keep doing your home exercises.
Call us if the dizziness gets worse or you feel unsteady.
Your next visit is in 6 weeks, on January 5, 2027.
Call sooner if your symptoms spread or you notice any weakness.
